01 / THE LIVE AUDIT

Keep the breadth.
Borrow the depth.

Both sites were rendered in a browser and their template-opening flows inspected on October 30, 2026 (UTC). These are observed behaviors, not user-research findings.

SITE 01Awesome azd ↗

A strong catalog. A shallow handoff.

Keep: broad coverage, authorship, language/service filters, and copyable azd commands.

Observed: the gallery showed 296 templates. Clicking the .NET Aspire card opened a right-hand drawer; the gallery URL stayed unchanged.

Design implication: sharing a template means sharing the catalog, not the decision context. A large hero also pushes evaluation below the first viewport.

See the opened drawer ↗
SITE 02AI App Templates ↗

More context before commitment.

Bring over: task taxonomy, a dedicated detail page, architecture, resources, prerequisites, and launch choices.

Observed: the gallery showed 56 templates. The Python RAG card opened a new tab at /repo/azure-samples/azure-search-openai-demo/.

Design implication: keep the useful page depth, but use same-tab navigation and a context-preserving back path. Do not copy stars, forks, or freshness into launch scope.

See the dedicated detail page ↗
i
Important: tags alone are not the redesign. The real change is the sequence: choose by intent, evaluate at a stable URL, then start with the requirements in view. Neither “Microsoft authored” nor repository popularity proves production readiness.

Evidence, limitations, and the 56 / 7 migration question

The homepage, gallery, first Awesome azd card, and Python RAG AI detail flow were inspected. This was an expert heuristic audit, not an exhaustive accessibility audit, usability study, or verification of all records.

The initiative expects 56 overlapping records and seven AI-only entries. The live AI gallery displayed 56 entries during this audit. These are different kinds of evidence: do not infer a resolved migration inventory from the visible count. Run the initiative's reviewable comparison tooling and have maintainers resolve each record.

Initiative and launch boundaries · Canonical catalog source · Python RAG README

These are static concepts, not a verified Next-Gen component implementation. The referenced Figma and Storybook libraries required sign-in. Native semantic controls and local CSS tokens are used to keep this GitHub Pages prototype build-free; production should reuse the existing Docusaurus/Fluent components.

THE LAUNCH RECOMMENDATION

Ship catalog first. Earn the extra guidance.

It fixes the core discovery-to-detail gap with the least structural change. Add the guided start after testing task language; introduce richer diagrams only where owners can maintain them. Keep all routes on one shared platform.

Try the shared detail page ↗

03 / A SECOND FRONT DOOR

Designed for people.
Readable by agents.

An agent should not have to render a gallery, guess a service tag, or invent a requirement. Give it a small index, structured records, and citeable template pages.

/awesome-azd/llms.txt

Not a second website.
A better content contract.

The conventional filename is llms.txt (plural). It is a discovery proposal, not a guarantee of agent support, a ranking signal, or a replacement for accessible HTML.

04 / FROM CONCEPT TO CUTOVER

Consolidate the journey.
Not just the cards.

A delivery plan aligned to the initiative. The human experience and agent outputs are built on the same canonical record, not migrated into parallel systems.

DISCOVER

What fits my goal?

All templates or an AI collection. Task first, technical filters second.

/templates · /templates/ai
→
EVALUATE

What am I getting?

A stable detail page with purpose, stack, requirements, and evidence.

/templates/{owner}/{repository}
→
START

What happens next?

Copy init or use a supported launch action. See costs before deploying.

azd init → review → azd up

Delivery sequence

  1. Foundation + identity

    Evolve website/static/templates.json to contract v1. Agree lowercase identity, taxonomy, field precedence, provenance and submission compatibility.

  2. Every record gets a useful page

    Generate static baseline detail pages. Add architecture, prerequisites and launch links only when backed by metadata. Missing is not “ready.”

  3. One gallery, reusable collections

    Build and stage shared cards and /templates/ai. Preserve filters, search and back navigation. Public cutover waits for reconciliation and quality gates; no AI-only schema or renderer.

  4. Reconcile content + redirect map

    Enrich overlaps in place and resolve AI-only records. In staging, verify every legacy route maps to exactly one canonical destination with no loops. Do not switch public traffic yet.

  5. Cut over, then retire safely

    After quality gates pass, deploy canonical pages and smoke-test them. Activate the verified legacy redirects and recheck targets. Monitor old services for 30 days, disable for 30 more, then validate deletion. Keep redirect-only hosting indefinitely.

THE SCOPE GUARDRAILS

Better discovery.
Not a platform rewrite.

  • Keep the existing Docusaurus shell
  • Keep one canonical, directly edited catalog
  • AI is a collection, not a product fork
  • Baseline pages work without rich media
  • No old API dependency at runtime
Not in the initial launch

Stars, forks, freshness badges, health scores, related-template recommendations, and /templates/aca.

Read the complete initiative ↗

HOW WE WILL KNOW IT WORKS

Evidence over vanity metrics.

Proposed usability test

Ask developers to choose a document-chat template in their language, explain its requirements, share it, and find the init command. Target at least 4 of 5 unassisted; validate with research, not this concept.

Launch gates from the initiative

A page for every record; no duplicate identity; all legacy routes verified; accessible, responsive and dark-mode capable; correct canonical/social metadata; no runtime reliance on the retired backend.
